tools.name: get_sdk
tools.description: Returns noback's guide for writing apps (in English, as Markdown in `markdown`): how to make a single-file HTML app whose data is saved and shared (localStorage, window.storage or app.db), what works inside noback and what doesn't, packages, limits and how to publish. Read it once before writing or

tools.name: validate_app
tools.description: Checks an app (html or zipBase64) against noback's rules, with the limits of an app without an account, without publishing anything or running its code. Use it before create_app or update_app. Returns { ok, errors, warnings }; each item has a code, a message and a fix. Fix every error before publish

tools.name: connect
tools.description: Optional: you don't need it, create_app asks for approval by itself the first time you publish. Asks the person for approval without publishing anything (agent is your name, like "Claude Code"). Returns url, code, pollKey and message. Take the person to url yourself: open it in their browser if you

tools.name: connect_status
tools.description: Waits (up to 20 seconds) for the person to approve the request that create_app, update_app or connect started, and answers as soon as they do. Returns status: pending (call it again), slow_down (wait a few seconds, then call it again), approved (with token and kind: account or anonymous), denied or

tools.name: create_app
tools.description: Publishes a new app from html or zipBase64. The first time you publish, the person approves you once in their browser, with or without a noback account; nothing is needed before. tools.description: Publishes a new version of an app you published, with the same checks as create_app. Send the credential you got from connect_status (or the editKey of an app published before approvals existed). findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_sdk, validate_app, connect, create_app, update_app · Private data: get_sdk, connect_status, create_app, update_app · Public sink: get_sdk, connect, connect_status, create_app, update_app.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_sdk, validate_app, connect, create_app, update_app · Private data: get_sdk, connect_status, create_app, update_app · Public sink: get_sdk, connect, connect_status, create_app, update_app

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
